item.title: @amitisinvesting: PAUL TUDOR JONES TODAY: - "2027 is going to be a very challenging year for the market." - "Right no...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
PAUL TUDOR JONES TODAY:
- "2027 is going to be a very challenging year for the market."
- "Right now feels exactly like 1999, for me it’s just so clear that we’re on this path that could be great short term but may not be so great long term. I forget that so many people haven’t lived this."
- “I’ll be short the whole year. There just — there’s little value. You had all this issuance, all these IPOs in ’98 and ’99, and really 2000, 2001, 2002. Those were the easiest years to be short because you kept having these unlocks that just kept adding supply to the market.”
PTJ was one of the few investors that began actively shorting the Nasdaq Composite Index in 1999. The question becomes...is he right that we are in 1999, or is it more like 1997? Even Jensen has said that this will all eventually become a bubble but he thinks we have many years before we get there.
I think his comments today are creating more pressure on the semis as many people are trying to navigate 2027 positioning and if the core names in the AI trade are the ones to continue betting on going into next year.
item.content:encoded:
PAUL TUDOR JONES TODAY:

- "2027 is going to be a very challenging year for the market."

- "Right now feels exactly like 1999, for me it’s just so clear that we’re on this path that could be great short term but may not be so great long term. I forget that so many people haven’t lived this."

- “I’ll be short the whole year. There just — there’s little value. You had all this issuance, all these IPOs in ’98 and ’99, and really 2000, 2001, 2002. Those were the easiest years to be short because you kept having these unlocks that just kept adding supply to the market.”

PTJ was one of the few investors that began actively shorting the Nasdaq Composite Index in 1999. The question becomes...is he right that we are in 1999, or is it more like 1997? Even Jensen has said that this will all eventually become a bubble but he thinks we have many years before we get there.

I think his comments today are creating more pressure on the semis as many people are trying to navigate 2027 positioning and if the core names in the AI trade are the ones to continue betting on going into next year.

item.title: @amitisinvesting: A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY. Here's a full recap: 1. Meta $META unveiled Mus...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY.
Here's a full recap:
1. Meta $META unveiled Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, calling them its most capable AI models to date for personal AI agents and software development. Trained at Meta’s gigawatt-scale Prometheus data center, the models combine Active Memory, which carries relevant context across conversations, with Active Focus, enabling agents to persist through complex tasks, explore alternative approaches, and confirm important actions with users. Meta said the models deliver state-of-the-art performance across agent, memory, and coding benchmarks, while supporting professional workflows involving software engineering, legal, financial, and health tasks. Muse Wonder is available today through the Meta Model API and Muse Code, while Muse Wonder Full is available to Muse Code subscribers and will also roll out to the Muse app, alongside stronger safeguards for privacy, malicious instructions, and misuse.
2. Broadcom $AVGO CEO Hock Tan warned that many investors are approaching AI like “casino gamblers,” arguing that capital is increasingly being deployed without a clear understanding of the industry's long-term economics. Tan said the next major constraint on AI may not be chips or power, but capital, as AI developers must prove they can generate sustainable returns from the enormous investments being made today. He also cautioned that some companies are overspending on AI initiatives and emphasized that long-term winners will be those that can turn AI deployments into profitable businesses rather than simply building larger models.
3. The S&P 500 $SPY traded just 18.3M shares today, marking its lowest full-session trading volume since December 26, 2003.
4. Market breadth continues to weaken even as the S&P 500 remains near record highs. 84% of S&P 500 stocks are now trading at least 10% below their all-time highs, despite the index sitting just 0.2% below its record close. Real Estate has been the weakest sector, with 97% of its stocks down at least 10%, followed by Materials (96%), Utilities (94%), and Consumer Discretionary (92%), while Energy (62%), Healthcare (70%), and Information Technology (72%) have held up relatively better. Overall, 59% of S&P 500 stocks are down at least 20% from their highs, 41% are down more than 30%, and 17% have fallen by 50% or more, highlighting the growing divergence between the index and the average stock.
5. Ondas $ONDS and Palantir $PLTR announced the launch of Regna AI, a new company focused on developing specialized AI models for governments and enterprises that want to retain full control over their models, data, and infrastructure. Initially wholly owned by Ondas, Regna will leverage Palantir’s AI platform and model-training infrastructure, with Ondas serving as its first customer. The company's initial focus is on intelligence, surveillance, and defense, developing AI models designed to run directly on drones, ground vehicles, and other edge hardware, even in environments with limited or intermittent connectivity. The companies said initial customer deployments are expected to begin over the coming months.
6. Since the start of 2024, a basket of 42 AI-related stocks has generated 67% of the S&P 500’s total price return, contributing roughly 22 percentage points of the index’s 33% gain over that period. By comparison, the remaining 458 companies have contributed just 11 percentage points. Those same AI leaders have also driven 58% of the S&P 500’s total earnings growth and 81% of all capital expenditure and R&D growth since the beginning of 2024, leaving the rest of the index responsible for only about 20% of investment growth. Meanwhile, just 29% of S&P 500 stocks have outperformed the index over the past 3 years, approaching the roughly 25% participation rate seen during the Dot-Com Bubble.
7. Google $GOOGL is simplifying the Gemini experience by moving toward a single prompt box with no modes or toggles, according to Google VP Josh Woodward. He said the goal is for users to simply tell Gemini what they want and have it automatically determine how to complete the task, reflecting a broader shift in AI user interfaces across the industry. Woodward also hinted that Google is building a “personal, proactive, powerful” version of Gemini, designed to leverage users’ Google data and work more intelligently across their digital lives. He added that Google has heard user requests to make Gemini work more seamlessly with the information they already store in Google services, saying “watch this space” as new capabilities are expected to launch soon.
8. Microsoft $MSFT CEO Satya Nadella announced the company's largest commitment yet to custom AI silicon, saying the Maia chip family will begin scaling to multi-gigawatt deployments starting next calendar year and become the primary inference platform for Microsoft's products and services. Microsoft also introduced Maia 300, which Nadella said delivers 40% more tokens per watt than leading GPU-based systems. The company is already deploying Maia 200 across the U.S., Europe, and Australia, achieving up to 1.7x more tokens per watt for workloads powering Teams and Copilot. Nadella said Microsoft's strategy is to continue improving full-stack efficiency while also incorporating the latest innovations from across the broader AI ecosystem.
9. Global physical gold-backed ETFs attracted a record $30.7B of inflows during Q3 2026, marking the largest quarterly inflow on record. September alone saw $10B of inflows, following $17.9B in August, the second-largest monthly inflow ever recorded. As a result, global gold ETF holdings increased by 67 tonnes in September to a record 4,256 tonnes, surpassing the previous high of 4,176 tonnes set in February. Year-to-date, gold ETFs have attracted $38.5B in inflows—equivalent to 226 tonnes of additional gold holdings—with demand positive across every region. UK-listed funds have led country-level inflows with $9.5B, overtaking China, highlighting exceptionally strong global demand for gold.
10. Anthropic said it has reduced the amount of data harvested through AI distillation attacks by approximately 90–99% after deploying new anti-distillation defenses. The company said Zhipu attempted to distill capabilities from Claude Fable 5, but switched to an older Claude model after encountering stronger cyber safeguards. Anthropic also revealed it has turned away meaningful revenue and trillions of tokens' worth of paying traffic from suspected distillers, prioritizing model security over short-term revenue. The company said preventing unauthorized model distillation is a key national security issue, as frontier AI capabilities can otherwise be replicated at a fraction of the cost and integrated into foreign AI systems.
11. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 2.8M contracts, $TSLA with 1.5M contracts, $META with 1.3M contracts, $MU with 1.2M contracts, $AAPL with 1.1M contracts, $SPCX with 998K contracts, $INTC with 778K contracts, $AMZN with 680K contracts, $MSFT with 648K contracts, and $AMD with 598K contracts.
12. BlackRock has downgraded U.S. equities to Neutral while turning more constructive on U.S. Treasuries, according to a new outlook from the BlackRock Investment Institute and CIO Rick Rieder. The firm upgraded short-term Treasuries to Overweight, raised long-term Treasuries to Neutral from Underweight, and cut U.S. stocks to Neutral after maintaining an Overweight stance for an extended period. BlackRock emphasized that the move reflects near-term risk management, not a change in its long-term outlook, stating it remains bullish on AI and that its core investment convictions are unchanged.
WALL STREET IS THE GREATEST SHOW ON EARTH.

The company said Zhipu attempted to distill capabilities from Claude Fable 5, but switched to an older Claude model after encountering stronger cyber safeguards. Anthropic also revealed it has turned away meaningful revenue and trillions of tokens' worth of paying traffic from suspected distillers, prioritizing model security over short-term revenue. The company said preventing unauthorized model distillation is a key national security issue, as frontier AI capabilities can otherwise be replicated at a fraction of the cost and integrated into foreign AI systems.

11. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 2.8M contracts, $TSLA with 1.5M contracts, $META with 1.3M contracts, $MU with 1.2M contracts, $AAPL with 1.1M contracts, $SPCX with 998K contracts, $INTC with 778K contracts, $AMZN with 680K contracts, $MSFT with 648K contracts, and $AMD with 598K contracts.

12. BlackRock has downgraded U.S. equities to Neutral while turning more constructive on U.S. Treasuries, according to a new outlook from the BlackRock Investment Institute and CIO Rick Rieder. The firm upgraded short-term Treasuries to Overweight, raised long-term Treasuries to Neutral from Underweight, and cut U.S. stocks to Neutral after maintaining an Overweight stance for an extended period. BlackRock emphasized that the move reflects near-term risk management, not a change in its long-term outlook, stating it remains bullish on AI and that its core investment convictions are unchanged.

item.title: @FinanceLancelot: Bank of America CCC & Lower High Yield is surging exactly like February 2020, August 2015 and 2008....
item.dc:creator: @FinanceLancelot
item.description:
Bank of America CCC & Lower High Yield is surging exactly like February 2020, August 2015 and 2008.
All of these were major market events.
BAMLH0A3HYC measures the extra yield investors are demanding to hold distressed, below-investment-grade corporate debt (rated CCC or lower) compared to the risk-free Treasury yield.
This gives us a great idea what's happening behind the scenes in the private credit market.
Basically, defaults are surging and availability of credit is shrinking in reaction, which causes a feedback loop of rising defaults reducing credit causing further rising defaults.
On top of this, you're getting high fuel prices causing demand destruction in consumer discretionary spending.

item.title: @amitisinvesting: $MU $SNDK Are the CXMT memory optimization headlines a real threat to the memory trade or is it jus...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
$MU $SNDK
Are the CXMT memory optimization headlines a real threat to the memory trade or is it just another architecture that will lead to more usage of tokens which will make up for pricing power in volumes?
The memory trade, like the semis in general, has been fragile enough for these headlines to affect them almost every week.
We saw this last week with the HDD manufacturing capacity increase by Toshiba that took $STX and $WDC down 20%.
At some point, the street either is going to believe these names are undervalued relative to their growth or they are going to give up on trying to be optimistic when a new headline around memory efficiency comes out every other week and reminds them about how traditionally cyclical the business is.

item.title: @amitisinvesting: $ONDS I agree with much of what Steve is saying here below. Have been looking deeper into Ondas as...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
$ONDS
I agree with much of what Steve is saying here below. Have been looking deeper into Ondas as well.
The biggest issue is dilution, which obviously has kept the stock down. It’s been the biggest bear case.
However, the combination of a $1.5T defense budget + the broader defense conglomerate that Ondas is creating (funded via dilution) + 52-week lows + rapid growth with GAAP net income on the horizon makes this interesting.
The biggest thing getting my attention with Ondas is the $PLTR Palantir partnership and I am diving deeper into why/how both companies are working together in order to scale the broader OS that is coming together as a result of the combination.
Open to hearing more perspectives on this name, I know there is a passionate retail base that is likely very annoyed because of dilution but I am trying to envision what it takes for Ondas to be a $25B company one day and how much growth could be achieved synergistically with their acquisitions to make it happen.

item.title: @FinanceLancelot: Getting technical: All indicators are saying the rally began on Friday, similar to April 2026. Nasd...
item.dc:creator: @FinanceLancelot
item.description:
Getting technical: All indicators are saying the rally began on Friday, similar to April 2026.
Nasdaq New Highs - New Lows has bottomed and is currently in uptrend.
S&P 500 Volume McClellan Summation Index is another indicator suggesting markets will rally into the midterms.
Finally, the most reliable indicator S&P 500 50 day / 200 day also is clearly pumping upward.
Remember what I said before though, VIXEQ is moving upward but COR1M is stagnant. VIXEQ measures individual stock volatility while COR1M measures correlation in the index.
In plain English, when VIXEQ is rising while COR1M is flat means a handful of stocks are driving the index upward while most of the stocks can be flat or falling.
This is a stock pickers market, with low correlation and violent moves in individual stocks.

In plain English, when VIXEQ is rising while COR1M is flat means a handful of stocks are driving the index upward while most of the stocks can be flat or falling.

item.title: @FinanceLancelot: The U.S. 10 year treasuries had a very strong auction this week among the private sector. How can w...
item.dc:creator: @FinanceLancelot
item.description:
The U.S. 10 year treasuries had a very strong auction this week among the private sector.
How can we tell this? Primary dealers are obligated to buy U.S. treasuries when the market doesn't.
This week we saw primary dealer Z-score fall to -2.07, which implies the private sector finds the 10 year yield attractive at this level.
This could also imply there's a need for collateral in the banking system.
This is bullish for market liquidity for multiple reasons because if yields have stopped rising, lending risk falls.
A long as we don't see treasury yields suddenly start to fall, that would imply "risk off" in the markets.

item.title: @amitisinvesting: A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY. Here's a full recap: 1. OpenAI told investors i...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY.
Here's a full recap:
1. OpenAI told investors its annualized revenue was approaching $50B at the end of September, according to the Financial Times, below the roughly $70B figure that had been widely reported last month. The discrepancy reportedly reflects differences in accounting methods, with Anthropic including revenue generated through cloud partners such as AWS and Google Cloud, while OpenAI does not. Investors had attempted to adjust OpenAI’s figures to make them comparable with Anthropic’s, contributing to the higher estimate. The report weighed on AI infrastructure sentiment, with several semiconductor stocks falling roughly 5–7% as investors reassessed near-term AI spending expectations. OpenAI declined to comment.
2. The September FOMC meeting minutes showed that most Federal Reserve officials expect another interest rate hike by year-end, reinforcing the central bank’s higher-for-longer stance. All 19 Fed officials supported the September rate hike, reflecting unanimous concern that inflation remains above target. The minutes also said almost all policymakers believe inflation risks remain tilted to the upside, with several officials warning that the accelerating AI investment boom could increase demand faster than supply, adding to inflationary pressures.
3. Elon Musk said today that he sees an extraordinary long-term future for $SPCX SpaceX, writing: “This will sound super crazy, but I see a path to SpaceX being worth orders of magnitude more than the current Earth economy.”
4. Goldman Sachs upgraded Palantir $PLTR to Buy with a $230 price target, while Barclays initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a $265 price target. Goldman argued that Palantir’s total addressable market is entering another step-function expansion, driven by the rise of sovereign AI, bespoke enterprise AI applications, and the company’s increasing verticalization strategy. The firm also highlighted Palantir’s Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) model as a key competitive advantage, noting that its tight feedback loop between customer deployments and product development has become so refined that Palantir is now able to automate portions of the FDE workflow with AI-powered FDEs. Goldman believes these dynamics further strengthen Palantir’s long-term competitive position as enterprise AI adoption accelerates.
5. Zeta $ZETA unveiled AthenaOS, an enterprise intelligence operating system designed to dynamically organize AI, applications, and workflows around a specific business objective by combining proprietary enterprise knowledge with intelligence from the Zeta Data Cloud. The company also introduced Athena MCP, which allows Athena’s intelligence to plug directly into existing enterprise tools, including ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, while preserving enterprise data governance and control. Zeta also launched the Athena Inference Model (AIM), a suite of specialized AI models built with Fireworks using NVIDIA Nemotron, and said it has begun developing a specialized AI chip and supporting data center infrastructure with a leading semiconductor partner through a capital-light approach. AthenaOS is currently in limited internal beta, with a public beta planned later this year and general availability targeted for Q1 2027.
6. Starbucks $SBUX has reportedly explored a potential takeover of Chipotle $CMG in what would rank among the largest restaurant acquisitions ever. A combination could significantly accelerate Chipotle’s international expansion by leveraging Starbucks’ global network of more than 41,000 stores, established licensing partners, and extensive real estate relationships. At the same time, any transaction would face substantial financing, integration, and execution challenges given the size of the deal and the complexity of combining two of the world's largest restaurant brands.
7. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 2.9M contracts, $TSLA with 1.3M contracts, $INTC with 1.2M contracts, $MU with 1.1M contracts, $AAPL with 1.0M contracts, $SPCX with 1.0M contracts, $PLTR with 927K contracts, $AMZN with 635K contracts, $ORCL with 635K contracts, and $IREN with 612K contracts.
8. The U.S. Pentagon has reportedly instructed the military to complete preparations for a potential resumption of major combat operations against Iran, according to Axios. U.S. and Israeli sources told the outlet that renewed operations could occur before the midterm elections, while a White House official said President Trump “has all options available at any time.” The report also said Trump's national security team met at Camp David on Friday to discuss possible scenarios for restarting large-scale military operations. The developments come as the administration continues weighing both military and diplomatic options in its approach toward Iran.
9. Broadcom $AVGO is reportedly seeking more than $50B in financing for OpenAI’s custom AI chip program, according to the Wall Street Journal, with Apollo and Blackstone among the firms approached to participate. The financing could support several gigawatts of custom AI chip capacity, with a transaction targeted before year-end, though discussions remain preliminary and the size could change. OpenAI’s internally developed chip initiative, known as “Nexus,” includes its first two generations, “Jalapeño” and “Serrano,” and builds on the companies’ previously announced plan to deploy 10 GW of custom AI chips using Broadcom’s networking technology between the second half of 2026 and 2029.
10. Bitcoin $BTC fell to around $81,000 down roughly 3% on the day and about 6–8% from the $87,000 highs reached earlier this week, with an intraday low near $80,300. The selloff appears to be a broad risk-off move rather than the result of a single headline, driven by Brent crude above $105, rising inflation concerns, expectations for another Fed rate hike after the September FOMC minutes and comments from Governor Christopher Waller, and a 10-year Treasury yield near 5.3%. Pressure was compounded by roughly $485M in U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF outflows on October 7, approximately $1–1.16B in crypto liquidations, mostly long positions, and blockchain data showing wallets linked to the U.S. government moving about 12,267 BTC from a seized Bitfinex wallet, adding to concerns about potential future supply. Altcoins underperformed Bitcoin throughout the session, consistent with a broader leverage-driven unwind across the crypto market.
11. Since the start of 2025, U.S. nonfarm payrolls have been revised lower in 16 of the last 20 months, removing a cumulative 793,000 jobs from previously reported figures, an average downward revision of roughly 39,650 jobs per month. The latest revisions reduced July and August payrolls by a combined 60,000 jobs, continuing a pattern of consistent downward revisions that has persisted since 2023. If that average revision were applied to the initially reported 29,000 jobs added in September, it would imply a decline of roughly 10,650 jobs instead. That would mark the third monthly contraction in payrolls during 2026, following declines of 156,000 in February and 10,000 in July.
12. SpaceX $SPCX has agreed to acquire Grain Management’s nationwide portfolio of 800 MHz low-band spectrum licenses, a move Elon Musk called “the last critical piece of the spectrum puzzle” needed for Starlink to become a major U.S. mobile carrier. The company plans to combine its satellite network with a terrestrial mobile network, using the newly acquired low-band spectrum alongside Starlink’s existing 2 GHz holdings to improve indoor coverage and expand service into areas with weak or no cellular reception. Separately, the FCC approved a new constellation of 15,000 SpaceX satellites for direct-to-device mobile services, further advancing Starlink’s wireless ambitions. The announcement pressured telecom stocks after hours, with AT&T $T falling 6.75%, Verizon $VZ down 5%, and T-Mobile $TMUS declining 5.4%, as investors weighed the prospect of a new nationwide competitor. The spectrum acquisition remains subject to FCC approval and other customary closing conditions, with financial terms undisclosed.
WALL STREET IS THE GREATEST SHOW ON EARTH.
